style_when: the article explains how a system, process or stack actually works — money flows, supply chains, pipelines, an agent assembly line
prompt: Clean isometric cutaway illustration of a laptop workstation on a machine shop workbench; its side panel removed to reveal two memory modules separated by a movable metal partition, the divider slid to allocate a small usable region and a larger reserved region. A small clock crystal near the processor is marked by a broken frequency trace. Thin consistent dark linework, flat muted palette of slate grey, cobalt, and bone white, one directional light from upper left raking across brushed aluminum and matte polymer surfaces. Wide 16:9 asymmetric framing, workstation off-centre left, deep negative space right, no text, no labels, no people.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, UI labels
rationale: Technical isometric cutaway explains the mechanism — firmware/OS partitioning memory and clocks — with visible hardware rather than a stock photo; it matches the site's engineering audience and avoids generic datacenter shots.
cue: The clock is a firmware decision
subject: a laptop workstation cutaway with memory modules divided by a movable partition
core_thesis: In November 2026 the two numbers a local AI purchase rests on — usable memory and sustained tokens a second — are set by the maker's firmware and the operating system rather than by the chip, so the box is now the un-auditable side of build versus rent.
core_conflict: firmware/OS-defined memory and clock throttling versus chip capability; opaque local performance versus transparent rental price tables
composition: wide 16:9 asymmetric isometric cutaway with the workstation off-centre left and deep negative space right
alt_text: Isometric cutaway of an open laptop on a workbench, its memory modules exposed beside scattered hand tools.
caption: A firmware-held memory partition decides how much of a local AI box's 128 GB the software can reach.
title: Your Box'S Hidden 79% Speed Cut

review.depicts: An isometric line drawing of an open laptop on a workbench, its lower chassis partly dismantled to expose a row of memory chips and circuit boards, surrounded by loose gears, a screwdriver, a metal file, a cutter and drill bits, with empty dark space at the right.
review.reason: The frame shows the article's own protagonist — a local machine cut open with its memory modules the visible object — matching the 'build versus rent' box story, though the movable partition is only implied and the gears/tools read as generic repair dressing rather than the firmware-audit mechanism.
